quests.name: Where Spirits Have Lease
quests.title: Where Spirits Have Lease
quests.description: It's your chance to buy a Benirus Manor
quests.notes:
It's your chance to buy a Benirus Manor

**Canonical Outcome:**
Anyone in town may tell you the rumor that Velwyn Benirus has a manor for sale right in town. He can be found at The Count's Arms inn between noon and midnight (at other times of day, he will be in his room upstairs). Velwyn will offer his grandfather's house, Benirus Manor, to you for 5000 gold and says you can take a look at it first.

1. Purchase Benirus Manor from Velwyn Benirus for 5000 gold.
2. Sleep at the manor just once, triggering an attack by ghosts. Kill them.
3. Read the scrap of paper on the ground floor of the manor, next to the glowing, broken vase. Pick up the paper and hand before progressing.
4. Track down Velwyn and convince him to help you break the manor's curse.
5. Take Velwyn to the manor's Sealed Portal so he can unseal it.
6. Awaken Lorgren Benirus and defeat him to lift the curse.
7. Benirus Manor will fix itself now that the curse has been lifted; it is fully upgraded automatically.

**What-If Crucible:**
You purchase Benirus Manor in Anvil for an astonishingly low 2,500 gold, only to discover it is infested by vengeful ghosts. (A) Uncover the secret altar, locate Velwyn Benirus, and defeat the ancient lich Lorgren Benirus: breaks the curse, restoring Benirus Manor as a pristine luxury mansion. (B) Embrace Lorgren Benirus's necromantic legacy: turns the manor into a personal subterranean laboratory for dark magic. (C) Sell the haunted manor to an unsuspecting merchant: offloads the cursed property for a quick profit.

quests.title: Whispers of Death
quests.description: Relay the prayers of the vengeful to ensure their vengeance is fulfilled.
quests.notes:
Relay the prayers of the vengeful to ensure their vengeance is fulfilled.

**Canonical Outcome:**
Go to Bravil and activate the statue of the Lucky Old Lady as if you were trying to receive her usual blessing of luck. Instead, the Night Mother will tell you that somebody has prayed to her and that you should relay these details to your Speaker. You will receive random combinations of one of the following people and locations. None of these locations are in Cyrodiil, so you cannot contact the person in question yourself.

1. Go to Bravil once a week and activate the Night Mother's statue to learn the details of somebody requiring the Dark Brotherhood's services.
2. Report these to Arquen in the Dark Brotherhood Sanctuary and receive your reward for the previous week's kill.

**What-If Crucible:**
As Listener, you receive weekly prayers from the Lucky Old Lady to assign contracts to Arquen. (A) Relay the prayers faithfully to Arquen each week: maintains steady Sanctuary income and establishes an orderly network of assassinations. (B) Suppress certain horrific contracts involving innocent children: quietly alters the Night Mother's directives, asserting mortal morality over cosmic death worship. (C) Exploit the prayers for personal blackmail before forwarding targets: doubles personal gold revenue while risking Sithis's supernatural retribution.

quests.description: The mini-quest to get your next contract from Ocheeva is titled "The Night Mother's Child". You will be directed to Skingrad to meet Fafnir, a Dark Brotherhood assassin posing as a doorman for a house party in Summitmist Manor. He'll provide you a key and some details on the party. Once you enter the manor, you will not be allowed to leave until the contract is fulfilled. Your objective is to kill everyone within Summitmist Manor, while the other guests are under the impression they have to look for a treasure. In order to get your bonus, you must not be observed/suspected by the remaining guests. All of the guests have a tiny amount of health, making them easy kills. When you have finished, return to Ocheeva for your reward of up to 600 gold (level dependent), and if you have achieved it, a bonus of the Night Mother's Blessing: a permanent +2 to your Marksman, Security, Sneak, Acrobatics and Blade skills.

quests.description: Rumors in Leyawiin indicate that there are strange animal noises coming from the house of Rosentia Gallenus. Upon entering her home, you will immediately find four 'Everscamps' hissing around the house. These are really just regular scamps that don't attack or do anything else other than hiss at you and have a different name. Rosentia tells you she has bought a Daedric staff recently and that is what's causing the trouble. She translated and read the "nonsense" word written onto the staff in runes, thus summoning the Everscamps. Now she is unable to get rid of the staff or the scamps. The scamps are not harming anyone and, if attacked, are easy to kill. However, they will reappear shortly thereafter. Rosentia will then send you over to the Leyawiin Mages Guild to talk to Alves Uvenim, whom she says will be able to help her get rid of the scamps.

1. Asking or listening around Leyawiin will soon enough produce the topic about Rosentia Gallenus.
2. Head over to Rosentia's house to discover what's been causing such strange rumors.
3. After you've been brought up-to-date by Rosentia, agree to help her with the problem.
4. First you must head to the Mages Guild and seek out Alves Uvenim whom Rosentia says will know what to do.
5. Upon speaking with Alves, take the Staff and your new friends and head over to Darkfathom Cave.
6. Make your way to the bottom of the cave, honing your skills on any undesirables you may encounter.
7. Once you've reached the hidden Shrine to Sheogorath you'll be prompted to drop the Staff and leave the curse for another adventurer.
8. Head back to Rosentia's and inform her the task is complete, she rewards you with the leveled Ring of Eidolon's Edge.

**What-If Crucible:**
Rosentia Gallenus in Leyawiin bought a cursed Daedric staff that causes four annoying Scamps to follow her everywhere. (A) Take the Staff of the Everscamp and deposit it in Darkfathom Cave to Sheogorath's shrine: frees Rosentia from the nuisance and earns the Ring of Sunfire. (B) Keep the Staff of the Everscamp in your inventory: uses the four immortal scamps as infinite targets for combat skill training. (C) Lead the four scamps into Castle Leyawiin's royal banquet: creates absurd chaotic disruption in the Count's court.

quests.name: Zero Visibility
quests.title: Zero Visibility
quests.description: Help the citizens of Aleswell
quests.notes:
Help the citizens of Aleswell

**Canonical Outcome:**
North of the Imperial City, the Red Ring Road runs east to west on the northern side of Lake Rumare. Aleswell lies on the south edge of the roadway, north northwest of the Imperial City, on a promontory that overlooks the Lake. It is a small hamlet with an inn, two houses, a garden, and a sheep pen.

1. Enter the Aleswell Inn and find the invisible innkeeper, Diram Serethi.
2. Explore nearby Fort Caractacus until you find Ancotar, the wizard in question.
3. Ancotar will give you a scroll to undo the invisibility curse. Keep talking to him (raising his disposition, if necessary) until he gives you a ring.
4. Equip the ring and read the scroll in the center of town. Speak with Diram once more.

**What-If Crucible:**
The entire village of Aleswell has been turned permanently invisible by the reckless wizard Ancotar in Fort Caractacus. (A) Find Ancotar, obtain his reversal scroll and ring, and restore visibility to Aleswell: saves the villagers from madness and earns free lodging at the inn forever. (B) Cast the reversal scroll without wearing the ring of protection: restores the town at the cost of permanently damaging your own magical attributes. (C) Slay Ancotar and take his spellbook: uncovers permanent mass-invisibility formulas, leaving Aleswell invisible forever.

[Remaster Image: File:SI-quest-A Better Mousetrap 03.jpg; File:OBR-quest-A Better Mousetrap 03.jpg; Grummite Shamans have taken the Focus Crystals] Sheogorath explains that he has chosen you to stop Jyggalag, the Daedric Prince of Order, from executing the Greymarch: an event that befalls the Shivering Isles at the end of every Era. Activate the ancient resonant resonator in Xedilian to restore the dungeon's psychological and lethal trials. (A) Recover the Crystal of Focal Justice, align the resonance nodes, and reactivate Xedilian: secures the realm's southern border and pleases Sheogorath. (B) Study the ancient architect's journals on psychological trauma: unlocks madness-inducing illusion mechanics before activating the machine. (C) Sabotage the resonator to disable the lethal spikes permanently: ensures Xedilian only drives adventurers mad rather than killing them.

Decide the fate of some greedy new adventurers in the Shivering Isles

**Canonical Outcome:**
[Remaster Image: File:SI-item-Resonator of Judgment.jpg; File:OBR-item-Resonator of Judgment.jpg; The active resonator; right] After having cleared Xedilian of Grummites, you will be approached by the dungeon master, Kiliban Nyrandil, who will thank you for repairing the Resonator of Judgment. Unfortunately, the Resonator has already drawn the attention of three adventurers, Lewin the Rogue, Syndelius the Mage and Grommok gro-Barak, and Kiliban tasks you with deciding their fate. If you haven't read the Manual of Xedilian, Kiliban can explain what's going on: :"The Resonator works by drawing adventurers to itself with a sort of magical "siren's call". Sheogorath uses the Resonator to find the "cream of the crop" as he calls them; the best of the worst to populate the Isles. Quite clever, eh? As the adventurers make their way through Xedilian's chambers, they will encounter choices that you make in these control platforms. Each chamber presents two options. When you push the appropriate button, an event will unfold for the adventurers to experience. One is physically harmful... usually lethal traps or creatures... something relished by the residents of Dementia. The other choice is more mental. They are designed to make the adventurers lose their grip on reality, much like the residents of Mania." Follow Kiliban around to each observation room. At each one, you will have the option of either Mania (resulting in insanity) or Dementia (resulting in death), which you express by pressing the smiling push-block on the right or the frowning one on the left, respectively.

1. Decide the fate of the adventurers.
2. Receive their loot.
3. Fight the Knights of Order.
4. Return to Sheogorath.

**What-If Crucible:**
Oversee the torment of three Cyrodiil adventurers navigating the reactivated chambers of Xedilian alongside Kiliban Nyrandil. (A) Subject the adventurers to psychological horrors (illusions, mad swarms, ghost giants) rather than physical death: drives them into glorious Mania/Dementia, satisfying Sheogorath's sadistic artistry. (B) Trigger the lethal crushing traps to execute them swiftly: spares them the agony of lingering madness at the cost of bloodier butcher's work. (C) Free the adventurers from the dungeon via an emergency escape latch: defies the Madgod's protocol, allowing three traumatized mortals to flee to Cyrodiil.

**Canonical Outcome:**
Fellmoor is a farm settlement along Pinnacle Road to the northwest of Xedilian and far southwest of New Sheoth. It is a major water root pod farming operation. The two Khajiit are the only of the four residents that actually work, however. Not only that, they are also persistently supervised in their work by an overseeing Altmer named Cindanwe. She will coldly tell you that their farming is of serious importance, and that there is a major problem concerning the lazy attitude of the two Khajiiti. Observing the constantly working Khajiiti makes it quite clear that the problem lies elsewhere. Speak to either one to learn that they are "the king and queen of the Shivering Isles"; although neither will trust you with any more information than that for the time being.

1. Speak with Ranarr-Jo in Fellmoor.
2. Gain the trust of Kishashi, in turn gaining that of Ranarr-Jo.
3. Dispose of Cindanwe by either killing her or wrecking her house.
4. Optional: Pick up Cindanwe's Notebook.
5. Return to Ranarr-Jo who gives you a reward for helping and a bonus if you retrieved Cindanwe's Notebook for him.

**What-If Crucible:**
Cindanwe, a pathologically neat Altmer in New Sheoth, is driving the paranoid beggar Hirrus Clutumnus insane. (A) Infiltrate Cindanwe's house and misplace five of her possessions to break her rigid obsessive compulsions: drives her to eccentric madness, pleasing Dementia. (B) Counsel Hirrus Clutumnus on how to ignore her neatness: attempts mortal psychotherapy in a realm that defies mental order. (C) Steal all of Cindanwe's meticulously arranged clutter and toss it in the bay: cures her obsession through radical sensory deprivation.

**Canonical Outcome:**
Asking around in New Sheoth will net you a few rumors about the ruins known as Vitharn. A map marker will be placed on your in-game map, due south of Fellmoor. Once you reach Vitharn, you will come across two groups of ghosts fighting each other. Blue tinted ghosts are defending the ruined fortress against their opponents, green tinted spirits that appear to be wearing Madness armor. Upon reaching the main door to Vitharn, you will see it is chained shut and surrounded by a ghostly aura; attempting to enter informs you that "The door is held shut by a supernatural force."

The ruined fortress of Vitharn is trapped in an eternal spectral loop of cowardice and defeat against ghostly invaders. (A) Correct the fatal mistakes of the four spectral defenders—arm the archer, steady the cowardly count, rally the soldiers: breaks the eternal curse, freeing Vitharn's ghosts. (B) Slay the invading spectral warlord Malfegor single-handedly: breaks the siege through sheer martial power, though the cycle risks restarting. (C) Absorb the spectral memories into your own consciousness: claims the ancient tactical knowledge of First Era battle at the cost of hauntings.

**What-If Crucible:**
Sheogorath vanishes, transforming into Jyggalag, leaving the throne empty as the sky turns into shattered crystal. (A) Cleanse the Fonts of Madness, forge the Staff of Sheogorath in the Font of Mania and Dementia, and claim the throne: assumes the divine mantle of the Prince of Madness. (B) Attempt to abandon the Shivering Isles and return to Cyrodiil to escape the Greymarch: tests whether a mortal can truly escape the fate of the Madgod. quests.title: The Roots of Madness
quests.description: Cleanse the Pools of Madness.
quests.notes:
Cleanse the Pools of Madness.

**Canonical Outcome:**
Travel to Sheogorath's Palace and follow the instruction of Dyus by attempting to imbue the Staff of Sheogorath through activating the Font of Madness. At this point in time, nothing will happen. Speak with Haskill, who will inform you that Font has been tainted by Order crystals. You must enter the Fountainhead and cleanse the Pools of Madness.

1. Attempt to immerse the Staff in the Font of Madness.
2. Speak with Haskill concerning the condition of the Font.
3. Enter the Fountainhead and cleanse the Pools of Madness.

**What-If Crucible:**
Order has poisoned the primordial Tree of Madness beneath the palace with dark crystals, draining the realm's magic. (A) Clear the corruption from the Fountain of Mania and Dementia, cleansing the roots with pure chaotic waters: restores the vibrant pulse of New Sheoth. (B) Harness the crystalline corruption to forge a hybrid weapon of Order and Chaos: creates an unprecedented artifact of balanced cosmic forces. (C) Overdose the roots with concentrated Greenmote: shock-therapizes the Tree of Madness, risking botanical collapse.

quests.name: Through the Fringe of Madness
quests.title: Through the Fringe of Madness
quests.description: Get past the Shivering:Gates of Madness
quests.notes:
Get past the Shivering:Gates of Madness

**Canonical Outcome:**
After first entering the Fringe, travel along the meandering main path until you reach the small town of Passwall. You'll quickly encounter two residents discussing the imminent fate of a band of adventurers that just passed through. Speak with the Redguard named Shelden, the self proclaimed mayor of Passwall, to learn of the nature of the Fringe and, more importantly, about the Gatekeeper found northeast of Passwall.

1. Make your way towards Passwall.
2. Speak with the citizens about the Gatekeeper and choose a method of disposal.
3. *Optional: Help Jayred Ice-Veins create some highly effective arrows.
4. *Optional: Eavesdrop on Relmyna Verenim and collect some samples of her tears to poison your foe.
5. Kill the Gatekeeper.
6. Receive the keys to Mania and Dementia and enter the Gates of Madness.

**What-If Crucible:**
Arrive in Passwall, where adventurers are slaughtered by the monstrous Gatekeeper guarding the gates of the realm. (A) Learn of the Gatekeeper's vulnerability from Relmyna's tears or bone arrows, and slay the titan: opens the Gates of Madness to enter the realm proper. (B) Lure an army of Cyrodiilic adventurers into the Gatekeeper's path to wear it down: sacrifices reckless fortune-seekers to breach the threshold. (C) Commune with the Gatekeeper using beast empathy: glimpses the tortured soul stitched into the flesh golem before ending its misery.

quests.name: To Help A Hero
quests.title: To Help A Hero
quests.description: Retrieve the Shivering:Pyke's Medallion
quests.notes:
Retrieve the Shivering:Pyke's Medallion

**Canonical Outcome:**
Off the northwestern section of Overlook Road is an unnamed road leading to The Isle of Flame. A little further than halfway down this path, it will split into two; take the right hand road heading northeast. At the end, you will come to the quiet settlement of Hale. Among the small community of artists is a resident named Pyke, who just recently came through the same gateway near Bravil that you have. Pyke explains that he was a former Knight of the Thorn in Cheydinhal. He will talk about the Count's son Farwil, from the Oblivion quest The Wayward Knight, during his explanation of how he ended up living in the Isles, among some other minor Cyrodilic references.

1. Speak to Pyke in Hale.
2. Head to the bottom of Fetid Grove.
3. Find and retrieve Pyke's Medallion.
4. Return the medallion to Pyke.

**What-If Crucible:**
Pyke, a former Knight of the Thorn, has lost his ceremonial medallion to the Grummites in Fetid Grove and longs for honor. (A) Infiltrate Fetid Grove, slay the Grummite shamans, and return the medallion to Pyke: restores his warrior dignity, allowing him to stay in the Isles with his lover. (B) Keep the enchanted medallion for yourself: claims its defensive wards while leaving Pyke brooding in disgrace. (C) Persuade Pyke to return to Cheydinhal and rejoin the Knights of the Thorn: encourages the errant knight to face his mortal past.

quests.title: Ushnar's Terror
quests.description: Shivering:Ushnar_gro-Shadborgob
quests.notes:
Shivering:Ushnar_gro-Shadborgob

**Canonical Outcome:**
Ushnar gro-Shadborgob is deathly afraid of cats. He keeps a lot of dogs to keep cats away. Unfortunately, there is a Khajiit beggar, Bhisha, also in Crucible who likes dogs about as much as Ushnar hates cats. Seeing as how Bhisha is a cat and Ushnar surrounds himself with dogs, Ushnar has a real problem and he'd like you to take care of it by making Bhisha "disappear".

1. Speak with Ushnar gro-Shadborgob.
2. Find Bhisha and either kill him or convince him to leave Crucible.
3. Return to Ushnar for a peculiar reward.

**What-If Crucible:**
Ushnar gro-Shadlog has an irrational terror of cats and wants the Khajiit beggar Bhisha banished from Crucible. (A) Persuade Bhisha to relocate to the cat-friendly streets of Bliss: ends Ushnar's panic without violence and receives an obedient undead hound. (B) Give Bhisha a stray cat to follow him around: terrorizes Ushnar with his phobia, driving the Orc deeper into hysterics. (C) Slay Ushnar to rid Crucible of an abusive bully: cleanses the district of an aggressive brute.

quests.name: Work is Never Done
quests.title: Work is Never Done
quests.description: Help Shivering:Tove the Unrestful
quests.notes:
Help Shivering:Tove the Unrestful

**Canonical Outcome:**
Tove the Unrestful can be found in Bliss, often at his home or The Choosy Beggar. When you first speak with him, he asks if you will continue to help him. His initial explanation for the strange greeting is that he keeps forgetting that people won't realize that he knows they will speak to him in the future, although he seems less than sure about even this. Regardless, Tove is quite secure despite his confusion and presses forward with his request. Tove explains that while he has perfected getting boats to float on the water, he has had less success in forcing the water to fly through air. Logically, a boat carried by flying water becomes a Skyboat. Tove requires at least 100 calipers or tongs to achieve the effect of keeping water airborne; he pays you five gold for each caliper or tong you bring him.

1. Find Tove the Unrestful in Bliss and speak with him twice about Calipers and Tongs.
2. Find calipers. Find tongs. At least fifty each.
3. Give them to Tove. After you give at least 100 total to him, speak with him again.

**What-If Crucible:**
Tove the Unrestful in Bliss is frantically building a sky-boat and requires massive amounts of calipers and tongs. (A) Collect and deliver 100 calipers and tongs from across Tamriel to Tove: satisfies his manic engineering dream and earns hefty coin. (B) Build him an authentic scale model of a sailing ship to prove the sky-boat's impossibility: tries to gently burst his manic delusion. (C) Steal Tove's blueprints and sell them to an eccentric engineer in the Imperial City: monetizes mad aeronautical theory in mortal Cyrodiil.

Whoever wears this hood takes on the identity of the Gray Fox: the wearer's fame, infamy, and bounty all become those of the Gray Fox. Any crimes committed (or good deeds done) are attributed to the Gray Fox rather than to the character wearing the hood. The cowl can be acquired at the end of the Thieves Guild questline by completing the quest The Ultimate Heist. See Gray Cowl of Nocturnal for more detailsThe blue writing down the middle of the mask says "Shadow hide [y]ou", which is also a farewell in conversations with members of the Thieves Guild. As is common in the Daedric Alphabet, the letter Yahkem (Y) is omitted from the inscription. Associated Quests: The Ultimate Heist.

If you are lucky enough to summon a Xivilai, it will also summon a Clannfear as soon as it spawns. items.notes: The Daedric artifact Wabbajack is a staff given as a reward for completing Sheogorath's Daedric quest. It transforms any non-NPC creature into another random creature for 10 seconds. It is highly unpredictable, as any gift from the Madgod would be. Only one creature may be Wabbajacked at any time (but you can repeatedly Wabbajack the same creature if you wish). If a creature is fatally wounded while Wabbajacked, it will transform back into its original form and die. If Wabbajack is used on a summoned creature and the summon spell runs out before the Wabbajack effect, the summon will remain in its new form until the effect ends, whereupon it turns back into its original shape and vanishes instantly. Associated Quests: Sheogorath.

items.name: Dawnfang and Duskfang

items.notes: Dawnfang/Duskfang is a unique leveled sword of Akaviri origin with a unique look. It is an unusual weapon in that it really is four weapons in one. During the day (6 a.m. - 6 p.m.) it is Dawnfang, doing fire damage on strike. During the night (6 p.m. - 6 a.m.) it is Duskfang, doing frost damage on strike (Both do the same amount of damage). At dusk and dawn, the blade in your inventory will be replaced with the other. Nourish Blade effect: Each weapon keeps track of the number of opponents killed with the blade; providing you killed at least 12 enemies during the preceding 12 hour period, the next blade you receive will be Dawnfang/Duskfang Superior. You must kill 12 enemies in each 12 hour period in order for the following weapon to be the Superior version. Killing your own summons is a good way to obtain the 12 required kills. Like other enchantments, the Nourish Blade effect requires charges in order to successfully activate upon killing the enemy. The Superior version does have an increased enchantment charge and absorbs health (Dawnfang Superior) or magicka (Duskfang Superior) in addition to the previous fire/frost enchantment. Kills are attributed to the blade only if the blade delivers the killing blow. Associated Quests: Baiting the Trap.

items.name: Staff of Sheogorath
items.specs: Type: Staff | Weight: 10 | Value: 8400G | Durability: 100 | Enchantment: Voice of Sheogorath in 75 ft for 15 secs on Target | Charge Capacity: 20000/1000 = 20
items.notes: The Staff of Sheogorath "freezes" all characters and creatures within the radius of 75 ft for 15 seconds and is functional both inside and outside the Shivering Isles. The Staff's spell will only take effect if an NPC or creature is attacking you, or another creature/NPC. It causes all affected targets to become paralyzed, but in a manner that is different from traditional Paralyze spells; rather than physically paralyzing them, the staff renders all targets unconscious and frozen in place, and no target affected by the staff can be damaged by attacks. You will, however, remain 'in combat' with any creature/NPC that was attacking you. When the spell is activated, Jyggalag's voice yells "Hold", and once the spell has deactivated, Jyggalag's voice yells "Release". Using the Staff is not considered a hostile act. The staff can be recharged using the Font of Madness. This is one of only two practical methods, given that it requires 20,000 magicka to recharge the Staff (the equivalent of 13 grand Soul Gems). The other method would be to use a Varla Stone. Associated Quests: Symbols of Office, The Roots of Madness.

items.name: Talisman of Abetment

items.notes: The Talisman of Abetment is a unique amulet that once belonged to one of the adventurers in Grommok gro-Barak's group. It will be found in the recovery chest at the conclusion of the Baiting the Trap quest. It is remarkably similar to Dawnfang's hilt, possessing identical orange gemstones, metal resembling scaled burnished gold, and has a distinctive serpentine-like shape. It was likely one of the Tsaesci relics that Grommok recovered from Trumbe, as detailed within his journal. As with many other leveled rewards, this amulet is generated in its container based on the player's current level when Shivering Isles is first loaded. Thus if a new game is started with Shivering Isles already present, such as the GotY edition, the player will always receive the level 1-4 version, no matter their level when it is actually found. This behavior is changed if you have the Unofficial Shivering Isles Patch installed. Associated Quests: Baiting the Trap.

trackers.name: Akatosh Transmutation & Septim Awakening
trackers.notes: Tracks Martin's psychological readiness to sacrifice mortal existence: (1) learns heritage, (2) confesses Sanguine sin, (3) rejects Xarxes promise, (4) dons Amulet, (5) accepts mortality forfeit, (6) manifests Avatar.

trackers.name: Oblivion Gate Incursion & Planar Bleed
trackers.notes: Tracks the widespread opening of Daedric portals across Cyrodiil's counties. At max ticks, roaming Daedra patrols sever trade routes and place county seats under siege.

trackers.name: The Great Gate Siege Countdown
trackers.notes: Tracks the critical 15-minute countdown during the Battle of Bruma. If it reaches maximum ticks, the Daedric Siege Crawler breaches the portal and razes Bruma.

trackers.name: Mythic Dawn Sleeper Network Paranoia
trackers.notes: Tracks civic panic, distrust of county guards, and the activation of covert cultists in the Arcane University and Imperial Legion.

trackers.name: Blackwood Company Hist Sap Intoxication
trackers.notes: Tracks the mental decay, hallucinatory violence, and aggressive municipal takeovers by the Blackwood Company across Blackwood and Nibenay.

trackers.name: Mannimarco's Undying Host Ascension
trackers.notes: Tracks the celestial conjunction of the Necromancer's Moon, the defection of rogue mages, and the expansion of worm anchor altars.

factions.name: The Order of the Blades
factions.description: The ancient Akaviri dragon-guard sworn to protect the Dragonborn bloodline of the Septim Emperors. Under Grandmaster Jauffre, the surviving Blades regroup at Cloud Ruler Temple to safeguard Martin Septim.

factions.name: The Mythic Dawn Sleeper Network
factions.description: The secretive Daedric cult dedicated to Mehrunes Dagon. Founded by Mankar Camoran through the Mysterium Xarxes, its sleeper agents infiltrated every county court and assassinated Emperor Uriel Septim VII.

factions.name: The Dark Brotherhood & The Black Hand
factions.description: The fanatical guild of contract killers worshipping Sithis and the Night Mother. Ruled by the Black Hand (one Listener, four Speakers), the Brotherhood operates from secret crypts beneath Cheydinhal.

factions.name: The Thieves Guild & Waterfront Syndicate
factions.description: Cyrodiil's organized network of cutpurses, fences, and beggars, led by the legendary Gray Fox. Operating under strict rules prohibiting murder of marks, they protect the Waterfront poor from Watch extortion.

factions.name: The Mages Guild & Arcane University
factions.description: The premier imperial institution of spellcraft, enchanting, and alchemy. Arch-Mage Hannibal Traven's controversial ban on Necromancy ignited a deadly schism with Mannimarco's Order of the Black Worm.

factions.name: The Fighters Guild of Cyrodiil
factions.description: The chartered mercenary guild providing municipal protection and monster eradication across Cyrodiil's counties. Champion Modryn Oreyn battles economic obsolescence against the ruthless Blackwood Company.

factions.name: The Blackwood Mercenary Company
factions.description: A heavily-funded mercenary consortium operating from Leyawiin. Powered by smuggled, corrupted Hist sap that induces berserk battle trances, they undercut Fighters Guild contracts and butcher villages.

factions.name: The Elder Council & Imperial Legion
factions.description: The ruling supreme senate of the Empire. Led by High Chancellor Ocato following Uriel Septim's death, the Council struggles to maintain civic order across Cyrodiil while provincial revolts threaten total collapse.

npcs.name: Brother Martin / Martin Septim
npcs.role: Priest of Akatosh / Heir to the Ruby Throne
npcs.motivation: Accept the burden of the Septim bloodline and atone for his Sanguine cult youth through total self-sacrifice to rekindle the Dragonfires.

secretsKnown.secret: In his youth, Martin was lured into a Sanguine revel house where a friend died during a dark ritual he chanted. He secretly keeps a rosewood Sanguine prayer bead in his breviary.

leverage.vulnerability: Guilt over his Daedric past and fear of becoming a tyrant like Camoran warns.
leverage.bribe: Absolution and honest spiritual counsel; immune to wealth.

dialogueHooks: Voice Tell: "Do not call me Majesty yet. I have not earned the word, and the word has not earned me. Let me be Brother Martin a little while longer."
Crucible Reaction: "If the party offers him absolution and support, he steps into the Avatar fire without hesitation. If shamed or isolated, his resolve falters."

stationing.role: Last Living Heir to the Septim Dynasty

npcs.notes:
**Character & Station:** Brother Martin (`character_brother_martin`), Priest of Akatosh at Kvatch; illegitimate son of Uriel Septim VII.

**Psychological Matrix:** Want: quiet atonement as a monk. Need: accept sacral monarchical martyrdom to save Nirn. Primal Wound: death of his companion Terennus during youthful Sanguine cult revels in Colovia.

relationships.notes: reciprocal of the tie recorded on the other side

npcs.name: Grandmaster Jauffre
npcs.role: Grandmaster of the Order of the Blades / Prior of Weynon
npcs.motivation: Fulfill his sacred oath to protect the Septim dynasty at all costs, even if it requires breaking his monk's peace and sacrificing every Blade.

secretsKnown.secret: Jauffre hid Martin in Kvatch thirty years ago without the Elder Council's knowledge, and hid the Amulet of Kings in an unwarded desk drawer at Weynon Priory.

leverage.vulnerability: The survival of the Septim bloodline and guilt over Blades fallen under his command.
leverage.bribe: Unflinching martial loyalty and ancient Akaviri relics.

dialogueHooks: Voice Tell: "Speaks in clipped, gravelly monastic tones that carry the unmistakable steel of a lifetime in armor."
Crucible Reaction: "Under extreme crisis, he draws Dragonfire's Edge and charges to defend Martin at the cost of his own life."
npcs.notes: **Character & Station:** Grandmaster Jauffre (`character_jauffre`), Prior of Weynon Priory and supreme military commander of the Blades.

npcs.name: Baurus
npcs.motivation: Atone for failing to prevent Emperor Uriel Septim's death by hunting down the Mythic Dawn sleeper network in the Imperial City.

secretsKnown.secret: Knows the secret labyrinthine tunnels beneath the Imperial Prison and the identities of high-ranking Mythic Dawn sympathizers in the city watch.

leverage.vulnerability: Survivor's guilt from the Emperor's assassination in the catacombs.
leverage.bribe: Verifiable intelligence on Mythic Dawn safehouses.

dialogueHooks: Voice Tell: "Blunt, watchful, never sits with his back to a door, speaks in low conspiratorial undertones."
Crucible Reaction: "Holds the sewer gates against overwhelming odds to allow the Hero and Martin to escape."
npcs.notes: **Character & Station:** Baurus (`character_baurus`), the sole surviving Blade from the Emperor's subterranean bodyguard detail.

npcs.name: High Chancellor Ocato
npcs.role: High Chancellor of the Elder Council & Imperial Regent
npcs.motivation: Maintain the brittle political integrity of the Empire and prevent civil war while refusing to pull Legion garrisons from the provinces.

secretsKnown.secret: Provincial rebellions in Morrowind, Black Marsh, and Summerset Isle are so severe that the Empire has effectively lost control of its outer borders.

leverage.vulnerability: Fear of an Elder Council coup or provincial secession.
leverage.bribe: Military reinforcements from county counts or provincial pacification.

dialogueHooks: Voice Tell: "Refined Altmer cadence, exhausted diplomatic precision, weighs every word as if drafting an imperial treaty."
Crucible Reaction: "Unsheathes battlemage lightning to defend the Elder Council Chambers when Daedra storm the palace."
npcs.notes: **Character & Station:** High Chancellor Ocato (`character_ocato`), de facto head of state governing from the White-Gold Tower.

npcs.name: Mankar Camoran
npcs.role: Mastermind of the Mythic Dawn & Prophet of Mehrunes Dagon
npcs.motivation: Cleanse Tamriel in holy fire and dissolve the mortal veil of Mundus so that Mehrunes Dagon can reclaim his rightful primordial realm.

secretsKnown.secret: His pocket paradise Gaiar Alata was forged from his own soul through the Mysterium Xarxes; slaying him instantly collapses the entire dimensional plane.

leverage.vulnerability: The metaphysical anchor tying his immortality to the Mysterium Xarxes and his twin children.
leverage.bribe: None; completely zealously devoted to Dagon.

dialogueHooks: Voice Tell: "Silken, hypnotic, cosmic sermons that weave complex theological heresies into irresistible promises of rebirth."
Crucible Reaction: "Laughs in transcendent ecstasy as his palace disintegrates around him, welcoming Dagon's return."
npcs.notes: **Character & Station:** Mankar Camoran (`character_mankar_camoran`), author of the Commentaries and arch-architect of the Oblivion Crisis.

npcs.name: Ruma Camoran
npcs.role: High Priestess of the Dawn & Daughter of Mankar
npcs.motivation: Serve her father's vision of cosmic rebirth and guard the portal conduits to Gaiar Alata.

secretsKnown.secret: She and her twin brother Raven are bound to an endless resurrection cycle in Paradise; killing one empowers the other until their anchor clock breaks.

leverage.vulnerability: Her twin bond with Raven.
leverage.bribe: Esoteric Daedric rites.

dialogueHooks: Voice Tell: "Fierce, fanatical conviction; regards mortal flesh as a fleeting illusion to be purified in blood."
Crucible Reaction: "Channels destructive shock magic into incoming attackers while shielding her twin."
npcs.notes: **Character & Station:** Ruma Camoran (`character_ruma_camoran`), daughter and high priestess of Mankar Camoran.

npcs.name: Raven Camoran
npcs.role: Inquisitor of the Dawn & Son of Mankar
npcs.motivation: Execute his father's purges while harboring secret doubts about the eternal agony inflicted upon the 'ascended' mortals in Paradise.

secretsKnown.secret: Raven secretly covets escape from his father's madness and will bargain with invaders if guaranteed permanent release from Dagon's grip.

leverage.vulnerability: Exhaustion from endless dying and resurrection in Paradise.
leverage.bribe: Safe passage to a mortal sanctuary on Nirn.

dialogueHooks: Voice Tell: "Brooding, cynical, glances at the blood gardens of Paradise with quiet revulsion."
Crucible Reaction: "If offered a true escape route, he lowers his daggers and yields the vault key."
npcs.notes: **Character & Station:** Raven Camoran (`character_raven_camoran`), son and executioner of Mankar Camoran.

npcs.name: Mannimarco, The King of Worms
npcs.motivation: Annihilate the Mages Guild, shatter Arch-Mage Traven's ban on necromancy, and absorb Traven's soul into a black soul gem to ascend as a cosmic deity.

secretsKnown.secret: Traven's sacrifice and self-imprisonment in a colossal black soul gem renders the bearer completely immune to Mannimarco's mind-control spells.

leverage.vulnerability: Hubris and reliance on the Necromancer's Moon celestial conjunction.
leverage.bribe: Colossal black soul gems or forbidden Ayleid relics.

dialogueHooks: Voice Tell: "Hollow, resonant, timeless chill like dust stirring over ancient sarcophagi."
Crucible Reaction: "Summons skeletal colossi and casts waves of death magic when his spell-absorb wards are breached."
npcs.notes: **Character & Station:** Mannimarco (`character_mannimarco`), ancient Altmer necromancer and leader of the Order of the Black Worm.

npcs.name: Mathieu Bellamont
npcs.role: First Blade of the Black Hand & The Traitor Defiler
npcs.motivation: Avenge his mother's murder by Lucien Lachance by systematically corrupting the Brotherhood's contracts and framing Lachance as a traitor.

secretsKnown.secret: He preserves his mother's severed head at Applewatch Farm and writes the forged dead-drop orders using her blood as ink.

leverage.vulnerability: The desecrated crypt of his mother at Applewatch.
leverage.bribe: None; consumed by psychotic revenge.

dialogueHooks: Voice Tell: "Smooth, obedient deference in public that curdles into sneering vindictive fury in shadow."
Crucible Reaction: "Leaps at the Night Mother's crypt with dagger drawn, completely heedless of mortal danger."

npcs.name: Lucien Lachance
npcs.motivation: Enforce the Five Tenets of Sithis, purge the Cheydinhal sanctuary of suspected treason, and protect the Night Mother.

secretsKnown.secret: He suspects that someone inside the Black Hand is poisoning the contract dead-drops, but remains blind to Mathieu Bellamont's deception until it is too late.

leverage.vulnerability: Devotion to Sithis and absolute reverence for the Night Mother.

dialogueHooks: Voice Tell: "Velvet, theatrical menace; appears silently from the darkest shadows when murder has taken place."

npcs.notes: **Character & Station:** Lucien Lachance (`character_lucien_lachance`), Speaker of the Dark Brotherhood.
npcs.faction: The Dark Brotherhood & The Black Hand

npcs.name: The Gray Fox / Count Corvus Umbranox
npcs.role: Grandmaster of the Thieves Guild / Count of Anvil
npcs.motivation: Steal an Elder Scroll from the Imperial Palace Library to break the curse of Nocturnal's Cowl and return to his beloved wife Countess Millona Umbranox.

secretsKnown.secret: The Cowl erases the wearer's true name and history from mortal memory; his wife believes he abandoned her ten years ago.

leverage.vulnerability: His love for Millona Umbranox and fear of dying as an forgotten phantom.
leverage.bribe: Heist tools, boots of Springheel Jak, and arrow of extrication.

dialogueHooks: Voice Tell: "Playful, aristocratic rogue cadence masking deep melancholy and desperation."
Crucible Reaction: "Leaps across palace rafters with supernatural acrobatics to secure the Elder Scroll."
npcs.notes: **Character & Station:** The Gray Fox (`character_gray_fox`), cursed bearer of the Gray Cowl of Nocturnal.

npcs.name: Arch-Mage Hannibal Traven
npcs.motivation: Protect the Arcane University from Mannimarco's worm cult, even if it requires offering his own soul as the final black soul gem ward.

secretsKnown.secret: His total ban on necromancy split the Guild in two and drove dozens of talented conjurers directly into Mannimarco's waiting arms.

leverage.vulnerability: Guilt over driving young mages to necromancy.
leverage.bribe: Rare Ayleid texts and Welkynd stones.

dialogueHooks: Voice Tell: "Grave, scholastic authority, tired eyes burdened by institutional decay."
Crucible Reaction: "Places the colossal black soul gem on his altar and drinks deadly poison to seal Mannimarco's fate."
npcs.notes: **Character & Station:** Arch-Mage Hannibal Traven (`character_hannibal_traven`), tragic reformer of the Mages Guild.

npcs.name: Modryn Oreyn
npcs.motivation: Expose the Blackwood Company's corrupt mercenary monopoly and uncover the dark substance driving their bloodthirsty frenzies.

secretsKnown.secret: The Blackwood Company smuggled an inverted Hist Tree from Black Marsh into Leyawiin and pumps corrupted sap into their recruits.

leverage.vulnerability: His duty to Guildmaster Vilena Donton and the lives of his fellow mercenaries.
leverage.bribe: Proof of Blackwood Company atrocities.

dialogueHooks: Voice Tell: "Gruff Dunmer pragmatism, loves painting terrible portraits in his spare time, calls fools by their names."

npcs.notes: **Character & Station:** Modryn Oreyn (`character_modryn_oreyn`), stalwart second-in-command of the Fighters Guild.

npcs.name: Captain Savlian Matius
npcs.motivation: Hold the burning barricades of Kvatch, protect the surviving civilians trapped in the Chapel of Akatosh, and reclaim Castle Kvatch from the Daedra.

secretsKnown.secret: Count Ormellius Goldwine was killed inside the castle; Savlian is withholding the news to prevent the surviving guards from despairing.

leverage.vulnerability: The lives of Kvatch's refugees.
leverage.bribe: Direct tactical assault on the Oblivion Gate.

dialogueHooks: Voice Tell: "Hoarse shouting over the roar of flames, sword dented and shield scorched, unflinching Colovian grit."

npcs.notes: **Character & Station:** Captain Savlian Matius (`character_savlian_matius`), hero of the defense of Kvatch.

npcs.name: Emperor Uriel Septim VII
npcs.motivation: Accept his foretold death with dignity and pass the Amulet of Kings to the prisoner chosen by the stars.

secretsKnown.secret: The location of his illegitimate son Martin, hidden thirty years ago in the Chapel of Akatosh at Kvatch.

leverage.vulnerability: The survival of Tamriel.
leverage.bribe: None; accepts his martyrdom.

dialogueHooks: Voice Tell: "Ancient, resonant, sorrowful majesty; sees beyond the veil of time into the constellations of destiny."

npcs.name: Ocheeva

npcs.notes: **Character & Station:** Marshal Isaura Venn (`character_blackwood_commander`), ruthless commander of the Blackwood Company.

npcs.role: Citadel Warden of the Kvatch Sigil Tower
npcs.motivation: Crush mortal resistance at the first breach and defend the Sigil Stone anchoring the gateway between Mundus and the Deadlands.

leverage.vulnerability: Daedric pride and disdain for mortal cunning.

quests.name: A Brotherhood Betrayed
quests.title: A Brotherhood Betrayed
quests.description: It appears that a Bradon Lirrian
quests.notes:
It appears that a Bradon Lirrian

**Canonical Outcome:**
There is a rumor in Bruma about Raynil Dralas, who claims that he is a vampire hunter. You also learn that he has already killed an alleged vampire in town, a local man named Bradon Lirrian.

1. Learn from townspeople about rumors of a vampire killing.
2. Persuade a local investigator and widow to talk to you about the murder of the supposed vampire.
3. Ask around about the whereabouts of the vampire hunter, Raynil Dralas. Many point to Olav's Tap and Tack.
4. After attempting futilely to speak to Dralas, talk to Olav to be given a key to Dralas' room, where you find his diary.
5. Give the diary to Carius, who points you toward Boreal Stone Cave. Travel there quickly, as you only have one day to finish the quest.
6. Kill Raynil, and take his keys to recover the Mundane Amulet from the waterlogged chest.
7. Take the amulet back to Erline to reveal its true nature; you may keep the amulet as your reward.

**What-If Crucible:**
Raynil Dralas posed as a vampire hunter to murder Bradon Lirrian and steal the Mundane Amulet. (A) Hunt down Raynil at Boreal Stone Cave, execute him, and return the amulet to Erline: clears Bradon's name and uncovers the true magical Phylactery of Litheness. (B) Demand Raynil hand over his co-conspirators' plunder before slaying him: extracts hidden treasure caches in Bruma at the expense of delayed justice. (C) Keep the Mundane Amulet without revealing its secret enchantment to Erline: exploits a grieving widow to retain an enchanted ward.

quests.name: A Brush with Death
quests.title: A Brush with Death
quests.description: Help a distraught Tivela Lythandas
quests.notes:
Help a distraught Tivela Lythandas

**Canonical Outcome:**
If you ask around town in Cheydinhal, people will tell you that Rythe Lythandas, a famous painter, has gone missing, and his wife, Tivela, is very upset. Go to the Lythandas house on the south side of town, and talk to Tivela for more information. Tivela tells you that Rythe had locked himself in his study, as he often did. However, after not seeing him for several days, Tivela decided to investigate. Upon doing so, she discovers that Rythe has disappeared.

1. Listen to rumors in Cheydinhal about the missing painter, and meet his wife, Tivela, in their house.
2. Tivela tells you about her husband locking himself in his room; go to his room, and enter the painting.
3. Find Rythe and he tells you about a thief who stole his magic paintbrush.
4. Find the thief's corpse and retrieve the paintbrush.
5. Return to Rythe with the brush and you will both return to Tamriel. He will reward you with the Apron of Adroitness.

**What-If Crucible:**
Painter Rythe Lythandas is trapped inside his magical Painted World by a rogue thief wielding painted trolls. (A) Enter the canvas, slay the painted trolls using turpentine, retrieve the magic brush, and paint an exit: saves Rythe and receives the enchanted Apron of Adroitness. (B) Study the metaphysical properties of the magic paintbrush: learns reality-altering illusion painting before returning Rythe to Cheydinhal. (C) Leave Rythe in the canvas temporarily to explore the painted realm: plunders the whimsical dreamscape, risking permanent entrapment.

quests.name: A Knife in the Dark
quests.title: A Knife in the Dark
quests.description: You must prove your worthiness to join the Dark Brotherhood
quests.notes:
You must prove your worthiness to join the Dark Brotherhood

**Canonical Outcome:**
You may overhear a rumor spreading in Cyrodiil about the recruitment of the group of assassins known as the Dark Brotherhood: "They say that when you murder someone, the Dark Brotherhood comes to you in your sleep. It's how they recruit new members." This means that in order to become recruited by the Brotherhood, you must murder an innocent in cold blood. Once you have completed that, the cryptic message "Your killing has been observed by forces unknown..." will appear in the corner of your screen, indicating that the next time you sleep in any given location, you will be visited by a member of the Dark Brotherhood. For suggestions on potential targets to murder, see this page.

1. Once you've murdered an innocent, sleep in any bed in Cyrodiil (see bugs).
2. Receive a visit from Lucien Lachance.
3. Travel to the Inn of Ill Omen, south of the Imperial City.
4. *(Optional) Speak with Manheim Maulhand about Rufio.
5. Confront Rufio and kill him; then sleep again in any bed.
6. Receive another visit from Lucien and join the Dark Brotherhood.
7. Travel to Cheydinhal and enter the abandoned house.
8. Speak the passphrase and enter the Dark Brotherhood Sanctuary.
9. Speak with Ocheeva and receive the armor of the Brotherhood.
10. Speak with Vicente Valtieri about your first contract.

**What-If Crucible:**
Lucien Lachance tasks you with executing Rufio at the Inn of Ill Omen as your initiation. (A) Execute the frail, terrified Rufio in his sleep: fulfills the test ruthlessly and secures induction into the Cheydinhal Sanctuary without incident. (B) Interrogate Rufio about his past victim: learns the wretched crime that placed the Black Sacrament upon his head before delivering cold justice. (C) Spare Rufio and stage his demise: defies the Dark Brotherhood at inception, earning Lucien Lachance's immediate nocturnal retribution.

quests.name: A Mage's Staff
quests.title: A Mage's Staff
quests.description: Complete your induction into the Mages Guild
quests.notes:
Complete your induction into the Mages Guild

**Canonical Outcome:**
After you have received all recommendations, travel to the Arcane University and speak to Raminus Polus. He will be in the Arch-Mage's Lobby during the daytime. At night, he will be unavailable to you. Once you are accepted into the guild by Raminus, speak to him about tasks to be told about the construction of your Mage's Staff. First you need to retrieve some special wood for the staff from Wellspring Cave, east of the Imperial City.

1. Speak with Raminus Polus about the Arcane University. Once accepted, your task is to have a personal Staff made.
2. Travel to Wellspring Cave only to discover there is a problem with the mages who guard this sacred place.
3. Make your way through the cave, taking care of (or avoiding) any enemies you encounter.
4. On the farside of Wellspring Cave dispose of the necromancers lying in wait.
5. Take the wood from the chest and return to Raminus, who instructs you to go see Delmar in the Chironasium.
6. Delmar asks you to choose the type of enchantment you would like and requests a full day's time to finish the work.
7. Return after a day has passed and Delmar will tell you to retrieve your custom staff from the cupboard in the back.
8. After you have your staff go see Raminus to be promoted to Journeyman.

**What-If Crucible:**
Necromancers have slaughtered the mages at Wellspring Cave to seize enchanted staff-wood. (A) Slay the necromancer infiltrators and carve your custom staff: secures your official Mage's Staff from Delmar and earns promotion to Journeyman. (B) Study the corrupted dark sap residue left in the wellspring: gains rare insights into Worm Cult enchantment at the risk of Delmar detecting tainted wood. (C) Pursue the fleeing necromancer couriers into the surrounding forest: intercepts intercepted communication intended for Mannimarco before reporting back to Traven.

**Canonical Outcome:**
Jauffre tells you that the Daedra are innumerable while the Bruma town guard are not. He therefore asks you to go and petition the other cities in Cyrodiil, the guilds and the Elder Council to send temporary relief troops to help close any Oblivion Gates that open around town.

1. This is an optional quest that can be done at any point after completing Bruma Gate and before starting Defense of Bruma. You can also partially complete it - i.e. get aid sent from some, but not all of the cities. Once you have completed the Defense of Bruma, Allies for Bruma will be automatically marked completed in your journal, even if you did not recruit everyone.
2. You are sent to request more troops for Captain Burd.
3. He tells you to petition the other cities, the guilds, and the Elder Council to send temporary relief troops to Bruma.
4. Go to each city and ask the count or countess of each for "Aid for Bruma".
5. After each city has provided aid, that city's troops will set up camp in Bruma.

**What-If Crucible:**
Jauffre asks you to rally garrison reinforcements from every Cyrodiil county to defend Bruma from the Great Gate. (A) Close the Oblivion Gates threatening all seven county capitals to secure full legions of aid: forges an unprecedented united provincial coalition for the battle of Bruma. (B) Focus on securing only the wealthiest counties (Imperial City, Skingrad, Cheydinhal): minimizes travel time and concentrates heavy elite armor, but leaves southern borders vulnerable. (C) Demand that counts send troops unconditionally under Imperial emergency decree: bullies provincial nobility, securing soldiers at the cost of deep regional resentment.

(C) Allow Falcar to attempt the soul-trap ritual on an apprentice: observes the dark resonance mechanics firsthand before disrupting the spell and taking the gem.

quests.name: An Unexpected Voyage
quests.title: An Unexpected Voyage
quests.description: The The Bloated Float Inn
quests.notes:
The The Bloated Float Inn

**Canonical Outcome:**
Go to The Bloated Float Inn in the Waterfront district of the Imperial City. Speak to Ormil, the publican, and rent a room for 10 gold. Head below the deck to your new room. Now you must sleep, but before doing so, move the pitcher to find a bag with some gems (see Notes section below). When you wake up, your journal will update to tell you that the Bloated Float has been put out to sea. Leave your room and you will immediately run into a bandit named Lynch. Talk to him (the correct options are the bottom of the two responses each time) to obtain some important quest-related information:

1. Sleep on The Bloated Float; you will awaken to find it hijacked.
2. Speak with Lynch about the gang now commandeering the inn and free the bouncer, Graman gro-Marad.
3. Speak with and kill Minx.
4. Speak with and kill Wrath to obtain his key.
5. Make your way to the cabin to find the leader of the gang.
6. Decide whether to kill her or negotiate with her. Negotiate successfully and she'll surrender herself and her sword; Ormil will apprehend her.
7. Rest again in your room: the ship will be back at the dock when you wake up.
8. Speak with Ormil about the gang to receive your reward in gold.

**What-If Crucible:**
While sleeping at the Bloated Float inn on the Waterfront, the ship is hijacked and steered out to sea by the Blackwater Bandits. (A) Subdue or slay Lynch, Minx, Wrath, and Ormil's traitor Selene: retakes the vessel bloodlessly where possible and docks back in the Imperial City. (B) Join forces with the Blackwater Bandits: turns pirate, sailing the Bloated Float into Niben Bay as a floating smuggler fortress. (C) Parley with Ormil and trick the bandits into surrendering their swords: proves cunning diplomacy over swordsmanship.

(C) Use merchant caravans as bait to trap Caminalda's accomplices: ensures total eradication of the highwaymen network at the cost of terrifying civilian merchants.

**Canonical Outcome:**
After you have fenced 700 gold and have completed the previous quest, Turning a Blind Eye, go to the Imperial City and wait for orders from the Gray Fox. Amusei should arrive shortly, and will give you orders to go to the house of Malintus Ancrus in Chorrol. You meet the Gray Fox once more, and he will tell you that you need to steal the Arrow of Extrication from the Court Wizard of Bravil, Fathis Aren. Once in Bravil, pay a beggar who tells you about Fathis Aren. You find out that Fathis keeps his most treasured items in a ruined tower outside of town. There may also be a secret passage from the castle to this tower.

1. Wait for Amusei to find you, usually in the Imperial City.
2. Go to the house of Malintus Ancrus in Chorrol and meet with the Gray Fox.
3. Go to Bravil and talk to the beggars for information on Fathis Aren.

5. Enter Fathis Aren's tower and steal the Arrow of Extrication.
6. Go back to Ancrus' house in Chorrol and give the arrowhead to The Gray Fox.

**What-If Crucible:**
The Gray Fox needs the key-shaped Arrow of Extrication, kept by the court wizard Fathis Aren in Bravil. (A) Infiltrate Fathis Aren's tower through the flooded grotto and steal the Arrowhead without slaying the wizard: upholds the Gray Fox's bloodless oath and claims a key piece of the grand heist. (B) Slay Fathis Aren in his personal sanctum: triggers a heavy Thieves Guild blood price but eliminates a dangerous Altmer conjurer. (C) Trade Aren a counterfeit arrow crafted by an Imperial City smith: deceives the court wizard while escaping with the authentic relic.

Only by sneaking into the fort and replacing his medicine bottle with the poisoned one, while remaining completely undetected, will you receive a bonus.

1. Receive the contract from Ocheeva and the new "medicine".
2. Travel to Fort Sutch and make your way to Roderick.
3. * (Optional) Remain undetected during the infiltration.
4. Switch the medicine with the poison in the cupboard.
5. Head back to the Cheydinhal Sanctuary to receive your reward.

**What-If Crucible:**
Roderick lies ill at Fort Sutch, guarded by loyal mercenaries, taking daily medicine. (A) Swap Roderick's medicine bottle with poisoned brew unnoticed: ensures a quiet, natural-looking demise and collects the bonus cleanly. (B) Slit Roderick's throat and butcher the mercenary garrison: leaves a gory calling card that puts Imperial authorities on high alert. (C) Inform the mercenary captain that someone put a contract on Roderick: triggers an internal panic, fracturing the warband while forfeiting Brotherhood standing.

quests.title: Bittneld and Emfrid
quests.description: Help to bring two lonely hearts together (non-journal).
quests.notes:
Help to bring two lonely hearts together (non-journal).

**Canonical Outcome:**
Author Casta Scribonia is well known for her romantic stories, but turns out to be equally romantic in life. When asked about Chorrol, she will tell you about two lonely existences in town, a guard captain and the proprietor of the local inn. She thinks they would be a perfect match, but will never reveal their names. The captain of the Chorrol guard, Bittneld the Curse-Bringer, seems to enjoy his work but isn't so keen on the town's female population. Ask him about Chorrol and he will tell you that although he thinks the women are "fine-looking", he also thinks they're snooty and not very nice.

1. Note: The quest is fully functional in Oblivion Remastered only. In the original game, most of this quest is skipped, instead going straight from Bittneld complaining about the town's women to Emfrid thanking you for bringing them together. The Unofficial Oblivion Patch re-adds the other lines.
2. Note: This quest does not appear in your journal
3. Talk to a local author who wants to play matchmaker.
4. Talk to Bittneld the Curse-Bringer about himself and his town.
5. Talk to Emfrid about Bittneld.
6. Return to Bittneld with a suggestion.

**What-If Crucible:**
Bittneld, Chorrol's lonely captain of the guard, needs encouragement to notice Emfrid, the welcoming innkeeper of The Oak and Crosier. (A) Play matchmaker through heartfelt conversation, bringing Bittneld and Emfrid together: brings joy and warmth to Chorrol's tavern. (B) Advise Bittneld to focus solely on military discipline and guard patrols: sharpens town vigilance at the cost of domestic romance. (C) Spread malicious tavern gossip that Bittneld prefers tavern wenches in Skingrad: creates petty town drama for personal amusement.

(B) Sell the enchanted Black Bows on the underworld black market: yields higher profits while arming Waterfront cutpurses. (C) Uncover the Black Bows' secret supply line in Rockmilk Cave: strikes at the heart of their criminal leadership.

Martin Septim requires the blood of a Daedric Prince—contained in an authentic Daedric artifact—to open Mankar Camoran's portal. (A) Offer Azura's Star, Wabbajack, or the Skull of Corruption on the ritual anvil: destroys a wondrous metaphysical relic to advance the salvation of Tamriel. (B) Seek out the most malevolent artifact (Mehrunes' Razor or Ebony Blade) to destroy dark evil: purges a cursed relic from the mortal plane while empowering the Septim ritual. (C) Hesitate to sacrifice the relic and seek an alternative conduit: buys time to experiment with lesser Daedric hearts, delaying Martin's portal preparation.

(A) Enter the haunted catacombs of Sancre Tor, free the four cursed Blade ghosts, and retrieve the holy armor: cleanses an ancient imperial tomb and earns the blessings of the Nine. (B) Absorb the divine essence lingering on the armor into your own blood: gains divine physical constitution before delivering the relic to Martin. (C) Plunder the catacombs of the Reman emperors alongside the armor: recovers priceless First Era imperial regalia, risking ancient ghostly curses.

The Gray Fox tells the tale of a famous thief, Springheel Jak, who died 300 years ago and was put to rest still wearing his enchanted boots. He then asks you to locate Jak's final resting place and retrieve the boots. The only known descendant of the famous thief is The Earl of Imbel, who goes by the name of Jakben and lives somewhere in the Imperial City. The Gray Fox finally tasks you to locate the Earl and search his house for clues.

(A) Confront Jakben in his ancestral crypt, slay him in self-defense when he reveals his vampiric fangs, and take the boots: secures the boots for the Gray Fox without violating guild rules. (B) Bribe Jakben with fresh mortal thralls: trades innocent blood for the boots, avoiding combat while descending into criminal depravity. (C) Expose Jakben's vampiric identity to the Imperial Watch: lets the guards storm Imbel Manor while you snatch the boots during the raid.

quests.description: You must help defeat the Daedra

**Canonical Outcome:**
As noted in Find the Heir, Martin will not escape with you unless everyone else in the Chapel of Akatosh can leave safely, but the guard will not let anyone out until Savlian Matius gives the order. Savlian is too busy killing the Daedra outside the Oblivion Gate to aid in your quest, so your only choice is to offer to help him close it. Tell him you want to help, get ready for battle, and activate the gate.

1. Talk to Savlian Matius.
2. Enter Oblivion. Head for the Blood Feast (the Sigil Keep) and make your way up.
3. Take the walkway to the Reapers Sprawl to find the prisoner. Kill his keeper to get the Sigil Keep Key.
4. Walk back to the Blood Feast, get to the top, and activate the Sigil Stone. The gate will close and you'll find yourself back in Kvatch.
5. Help Savlian clear out the Daedra in the plaza in front of the chapel so the survivors inside can be rescued.
6. Talk to Martin and tell him to follow you to Weynon Priory.

**What-If Crucible:**
Kvatch is engulfed in Daedric hellfire, and Savlian Matius needs a champion to enter the colossal Oblivion Gate. (A) Charge through the gate, climb the Sigil Keep, and sever the Sigil Stone from its magma cradle: collapses the gate, saves Kvatch survivors, and earns the title 'Hero of Kvatch'. (B) Rally the city guards into a defensive perimeter outside while you breach the gate alone: minimizes mortal casualties at the cost of facing Dremora lords in solo combat. (C) Loot the Daedric spires for rare Sigil Stones and dark armor before closing the portal: amasses incredible magical wealth while Kvatch's Chapel of Akatosh hangs by a thread.

quests.description: Speak to Falcar in the Cheydinhal Mages Guild for a recommendation. He wants you to find a Ring of Burden an Associate recently lost. He suspects it was thrown down the guild well and says you'll need a key to get in; Deetsan—another guild member—has one. Deetsan will agree to talk to you about your assignment only if Falcar is not in the same room, which is the case between 1pm and 6pm. Once he's out of sight, you'll learn you're not the first one to get this task. Vidkun - the previous Associate - disappeared while trying to find the ring. After this word of caution, Deetsan will give you the Well Key and a Buoyancy spell.

Speak to Falcar in the Cheydinhal Mages Guild for a recommendation. He wants you to find a Ring of Burden an Associate recently lost. He suspects it was thrown down the guild well and says you'll need a key to get in; Deetsan—another guild member—has one. Deetsan will agree to talk to you about your assignment only if Falcar is not in the same room, which is the case between 1pm and 6pm. 1. Speak with Falcar, the head of the Cheydinhal Mages Guild, who asks you to find his lost ring.
2. Go see Deetsan to obtain a key to the outside well and a Buoyancy spell.
3. Retrieve the ring from the well and speak with Deetsan again.
4. Search Falcar's room for your recommendation, but find evidence of Necromancy instead.
5. Speak once again with Deetsan and she will agree to write your recommendation for you.

**What-If Crucible:**
Falcar sends you to retrieve a heavy Ring of Burden from the bottom of a flooded well, where an apprentice drowned. (A) Cast Buoyancy, retrieve the Ring of Burden, and expose Falcar's murder of Vidkun: forces Falcar to flee Cheydinhal and secures Deetsan's recommendation. (B) Search Falcar's private chambers to find his stash of Black Soul Gems: provides the Council with damning proof of necromancy within guild ranks. (C) Keep the Ring of Burden and use it as a lethal drowning weapon: exploits the enchanted artifact while disguising your discovery of Falcar's treason.

quests.name: Clavicus Vile
quests.title: Clavicus Vile
quests.description: Retrieve the infamous sword Umbra (sword)
quests.notes:
Retrieve the infamous sword Umbra (sword)

**Canonical Outcome:**
The shrine is located in the West Weald, a bit off the east of the Gold Road as it travels south, near Lake Rumare, and between Fort Virtue and the Ayleid ruin, Ceyatatar. You must find the shrine on your own; no one will tell you where it is.

1. Present Clavicus Vile with 500 gold once you reach level 20.
2. Clavicus will tell you that he wants the sword containing the soul of the warrior Umbra.
3. Retrieve the Umbra sword from the Bosmer, Umbra, located in the Ayleid ruin Vindasel.
4. Note: Umbra may be killed, and the sword retrieved, at any level, and even before initiating the quest. Once Umbra is dead and the sword is in your possession, speak with Ma'Raska to initiate the quest, then approach the shrine of Clavicus Vile.
5. Return to the shrine for your reward, the Masque of Clavicus Vile. Alternatively, you can refuse to give Umbra to Clavicus Vile, and you get to keep the sword as your reward.

**What-If Crucible:**
Clavicus Vile wants the soul-stealing sword Umbra, but his hound Barbas begs you not to deliver it. (A) Slay Umbra in Vindasel and return the cursed sword to Clavicus Vile: receives the Masque of Clavicus Vile and restores the Prince's full power. (B) Heed Barbas's desperate warning, keep the sword Umbra, and walk away: retains Tamriel's deadliest soul-trapping longsword while spurning the Prince of Bargains. (C) Redeem Lenwin (Umbra) by using restoration magic to break the sword's psychic grip: frees the warrior's soul from the blade's curse.

1. Traven promotes you to Arch-Mage and then soul traps himself into the Colossal Black Soul Gem.
2. Take the gem and travel to Echo Cave.
3. Make your way through the cave until you reach Mannimarco.
4. Talk with him for a while, then kill him.
5. Return to the University triumphant. The Arch-Mage's quarters are yours!

**What-If Crucible:**
Arch-Mage Hannibal Traven sacrifices his soul into the Colossal Black Soul Gem to shield you from Mannimarco. (A) March into Echo Cave and slay the King of Worms Mannimarco: eradicates the necromantic threat, becomes the Arch-Mage of Cyrodiil, and claims the Staff of Worms. (B) Attempt to bind Mannimarco's essence into the Colossal Gem alongside Traven: traps both arch-mages in eternal metaphysical stasis, preventing future resurrections. (C) Offer Mannimarco an uneasy truce in exchange for the secrets of eternal lichdom: betrays Traven's sacrifice and ushers in an era of shadow within the Arcane University.

**What-If Crucible:**
Olyn Seran at the Molag Bal shrine tests your ability to bind and summon a high-tier Faded Wraith. (B) Bind two divergent extraplanar entities simultaneously: pushes the limits of mortal summoning, risking an extraplanar breach at the shrine. (C) Banish a wild summoned Daedra that attacks the shrine: earns Olyn's admiration by rectifying another summoner's catastrophic mistake.

quests.name: Corruption and Conscience
quests.title: Corruption and Conscience
quests.description: The corruption started when the new captain of the guard, Ulrich Leland, arrived in Cheydinhal. Ask about "Rumors" in Cheydinhal and you'll learn the topic "Fines". Ask about the exorbitant fines and you'll be directed to the outspoken Llevana Nedaren to help fight the corruption. She tells you to seek out Garrus Darelliun in the Count's Castle. When you talk to him, ask him about Ulrich. You'll need a disposition of at least 60 with him before he'll tell you anything. Garrus tells you that he needs a witness to be able to bring the case before the Count. He directs you to Aldos Othran, a local drunk that lost his house after being unable to pay the various fines imposed on him by Ulrich.

Ask about the exorbitant fines and you'll be directed to the outspoken Llevana Nedaren to help fight the corruption. She tells you to seek out Garrus Darelliun in the Count's Castle. 1. Learn of the corruption in the guards, and speak to Llevana Nedaren to help fight it.
2. Nedaren points you to Garrus Darelliun, who will direct you to Aldos Othran when asked about Ulrich.
3. Speak with Othran, and he'll have an altercation with a guard in which he is killed.
4. Leave, and speak with Llevana who tells you to bring Ulrich to her.
5. Before you bring Ulrich to Llevana, speak with Garrus for an alternate method.
6. Decide which method to take.
7. When Ulrich is dealt with, you receive your gold and single fame/infamy point.

**What-If Crucible:**
Captain Ulrich Leland is imposing exorbitant, ruinous fines on Cheydinhal citizens, driving Llevana Nedaren to vengeance. (A) Gather evidence with Garrus Darelliun to expose Ulrich legally, putting him in prison: preserves justice without bloodshed and promotes Garrus. (B) Allow Llevana Nedaren to lure Ulrich to her home and feed him to her pet rats: delivers visceral poetic vengeance at the cost of Llevana's soul. (C) Blackmail Ulrich for a portion of the extortion money: profits off the suffering of Cheydinhal's citizens.

quests.title: Dagon Shrine
quests.description: Find and infiltrate the Mythic Dawn
quests.notes:
Find and infiltrate the Mythic Dawn

**Canonical Outcome:**
You've finally been able to track down the location of Mythic Dawn's secret shrine to Mehrunes Dagon. The location, marked on your map, is in the northeastern part of the province at Lake Arrius Caverns, just north of Cheydinhal. Unlike Weynon Priory and Kvatch, you cannot immediately fast travel to Lake Arrius unless you happen to have been there before.

1. Travel to the secret Mythic Dawn shrine in Lake Arrius Caverns.
2. Steal the Mysterium Xarxes.
3. Return to Martin in the Great Hall of Cloud Ruler Temple.

**What-If Crucible:**
Infiltrate the Mythic Dawn's secret subterranean cavern in Lake Arrius to steal the Mysterium Xarxes. (A) Play along with Harrow, don the cult robes, and rescue the sacrificial captive Jeelius while seizing the Mysterium Xarxes: deals a devastating blow to Mankar Camoran and saves an innocent. (B) Execute the Argonian sacrifice on Dagon's altar to cement your deep cover: allows you to walk out with the holy book unchallenged, but stains your hands with innocent blood. (C) Slay Harrow and charge into the temple with unsheathed steel: slaughters the entire Mythic Dawn coven in a blazing bloodbath, collapsing the cavern roof.

(B) Decline respectfully: maintains mortal humanity and paladin compatibility while preserving Vicente's mentorship. (C) Betray Vicente's vampiric nature to the Order of the Virtuous Blood: sparks a clandestine purge within Cheydinhal, compromising the Sanctuary.

quests.title: Deliver the Amulet
quests.description: You must deliver the Amulet of Kings
quests.notes:
You must deliver the Amulet of Kings

**Canonical Outcome:**
After exiting the sewers, your first task is to deliver the Amulet of Kings to Jauffre, the Grandmaster of the Blades. He resides at Weynon Priory, immediately south of Chorrol. Of course, you can postpone this task indefinitely and complete it at your leisure. However, Oblivion gates will not open until you complete Find the Heir (except the initial one at Kvatch, which will be active immediately after the beginning of the game), and you will get a free horse when you deliver the Amulet.

1. Travel to Weynon Priory, near Chorrol.
2. Go inside and speak to Jauffre.

**What-If Crucible:**
Following Emperor Uriel Septim VII's assassination, you must deliver the Amulet of Kings to Jauffre at Weynon Priory. (A) Travel swiftly across the Great Forest and deliver the Amulet directly into Jauffre's hands: secures the imperial heirloom and alerts the Grandmaster of the Blades without delay. (B) Seek audience with High Chancellor Ocato in the Imperial Palace first: informs the Elder Council of the Emperor's demise, navigating imperial political panic. (C) Attempt to wear the Amulet of Kings yourself: confirms that non-Dragonborn cannot wear the relic, reinforcing the divine prophecy.

quests.name: Den of Thieves
quests.title: Den of Thieves
quests.description: A gang of Bosmer thieves has been causing some problems around Anvil
quests.notes:
A gang of Bosmer thieves has been causing some problems around Anvil

**Canonical Outcome:**
You can receive this contract from Azzan in the Anvil Fighters Guild after you've done a few jobs for Modryn Oreyn in Chorrol. He'll ask you to look for a den of thieves that has been responsible for a recent spate of thefts in the area, referencing your past contract to help Norbert Lelles: "Good to see you're working hard. I've got some more thieves for you to deal with in Anvil. There have been a number of thefts in the area, and witnesses believe the thieves are holed up nearby. Check around, and see what you can learn." Azzan pairs you up for this mission with Maglir, whom you met recently on a past contract: "I'm not sure the numbers you'll be dealing with, so I'm sending you with another new recruit. Maglir. I believe you two have already met."

1. Receive the quest details from Azzan.
2. Discuss the contract with Maglir.
3. Speak with Newheim the Portly to receive additional details and an optional mini-quest.
4. Kill the thieves in Hrota Cave and (optionally) retrieve Newheim's Heirloom.
5. Return to Azzan and Newheim for your rewards.

**What-If Crucible:**
A gang of thieves is terrorizing Anvil, and Azzan pairs you with the disgruntled, unreliable Maglir to track them down. (A) Sweep Hrota Cave, eliminate the thief ring, and cover for Maglir's cowardice in your report: maintains guild cohesion and secures Azzan's respect. (B) Report Maglir's laziness and failure to engage directly to Azzan: initiates the disciplinary disciplinary spiral that drives Maglir into the Blackwood Company. (C) Cut a secret deal with the thieves' leader: takes a portion of their stolen plunder to steer guild patrols away from Hrota Cave.

quests.description: Find out why several of your guildmates are causing trouble in Leyawiin

Find out why several of your guildmates are causing trouble in Leyawiin

**Canonical Outcome:**
After completing Unfinished Business, Modryn Oreyn gives you your next duty. Your fellow guildmates Dubok gro-Shagk, Rellian, and Vantus Prelius have apparently been getting rowdy at a tavern in Leyawiin, which is bringing the guild into disrepute. You're to head south to find out what's going on.

2. Speak with the guildmates and the barkeep at Five Claws Lodge and learn of their frustrations.
3. Talk to Margarte regarding contracts.
4. Collect Ectoplasm to convince Margarte of the Fighters Guild's reliability.
5. Update the guild members on the latest developments.
6. Return to Modryn Oreyn for your reward.

**What-If Crucible:**
Three drunken guild members are brawling and terrorizing Leyawiin's Five Claws Lodge due to lack of employment. (A) Negotiate a contract with Margarte to hire the trio as ogre tooth and minotaur horn suppliers: restores order in Leyawiin and provides the fighters with honorable, productive labor. (B) Beat the unruly guild members unconscious in tavern combat: proves physical dominance through brawn, intimidating them into quiet obedience. (C) Frame the Blackwood Company for inciting the tavern riot: sparks citywide street violence between the rival mercenary guilds.

quests.title: Fingers of the Mountain
quests.description: Sort out a problem with a former Mages Guild
quests.notes:
Sort out a problem with a former Mages Guild

**Canonical Outcome:**
Speak to Teekeeus in the Chorrol Mages Guild about a recommendation, and you will receive instructions to find out what is bothering Earana - an excommunicated sorcerer. In short, Teekeeus just wants her out of town to avoid any trouble.

1. Speak with Teekeeus. He wants you to find out why Earana - an expelled mage - is hanging around town.
2. Find Earana around town and speak with her to be asked for help in retrieving a book.
3. Return to Teekeeus. He tells you to bring the book directly to him instead.
4. Travel north up the mountain to Cloud Top and retrieve the book.
5. At this point, you can either give the book to Teekeeus or Earana:
6. * If given to Teekeeus, Earana will ask you to steal it back (if you say no the quest will end here).
7. * If given to Earana, you will be asked to steal it back by Teekeeus (but wait until Earana gives you her notes first).
8. * Either way you will receive the Chorrol Recommendation.
9. Afterwards, take the note from Earana and head back to Cloud Top. Follow the instructions below to gain the Finger of the Mountain spell. (optional)

**What-If Crucible:**
Both Earana and Teekeeus vie for the ancient tome 'Fingers of the Mountain' found on Cloud Top. (A) Hand the tome to Teekeeus: upholds orthodox guild discipline, earns his recommendation, and keeps dangerous shock magic out of reckless hands. (B) Hand the tome to Earana: unlocks the catastrophic 'Fingers of the Mountain' lightning spell at the cost of disciplinary tension with Teekeeus. (C) Steal the tome back from Teekeeus after getting the recommendation and give it to Earana: plays both factions against each other, maximizing magical power and guild standing.
